output.name: Lamet

anatomy.part: crown of the kite, the top of the frame
lower corner of the kite body
the name-knot where the cloth strip is tied to the tail
end of the name-strip, flicking left
a loose ribbon flutter off the tail

output.myth: When old Tenu went aloft, his grandchildren sewed his name onto a strip of sailcloth, one knot for each letter. They flew it at midsummer, when the light stays late. Ennu the Kite-Wright had built the frame, and Aun had shown him how to bend it, the way Aun shows everyone things, without asking first. The name-kite climbs the Lamp Road with its tail behind, so every star that sees it knows who is passing. Tavo came over the north ridge to tear the strip, because Tavo laughs at names and cannot be bargained with. The children held the reel and sang. Hesk, at the pole, did not look up. She keeps count. She marks each name as it passes her string and lets none of them go. The strip is knotted to the bright star at the tail, and that is where the name stays when the cloth wears thin. So we tie our names on. The wind does not read. Hesk does.
output.verse:
A cloth strip climbs slow
up the road; Hesk keeps the name
one knot in the wind
